boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Emerson study environments, from designated quiet library areas to reservable rooms and campus-center spaces.

cards.title: West Stacks
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Set up here for work that needs silence: Emerson designates the entire West Stacks as a quiet study area with no conversations.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent-study area in the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s library code identifies the entire West Stacks as a quiet study area where conversations and other noise are not allowed.
cards.source_title: Library Code of Conduct | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Follow library conduct rules and posted closing times; College ID may be requested.

cards.title: 6th Floor Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from a quiet setting; the sixth-floor carrels are designated for silent study.
cards.short_summary: Individual carrels in a library-designated quiet zone.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s library code lists the sixth-floor study carrels as quiet study areas where conversations and other noise are not allowed.
cards.source_title: Library Code of Conduct | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Follow library conduct rules and posted closing times; College ID may be requested.

cards.title: Presidents Room Large Tables
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Meet a small project group at the large tables, keeping conversation low enough not to disturb nearby library users.
cards.short_summary: Large tables designated by the library for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s library code directs group study to the large tables in the Presidents Room and asks users to keep conversations low.
cards.source_title: Library Code of Conduct | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Use for group study and keep conversations low; follow posted library closing times.

cards.title: Library Entrance Large Tables
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Choose these large tables for collaborative coursework, then keep voices low and leave the shared area ready for the next group.
cards.short_summary: A group-study table area near the library entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s library code identifies the large tables near the entrance as a place for group study.
cards.source_title: Library Code of Conduct | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Use for group study and keep conversations low; follow posted library closing times.

cards.title: Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Reserve a room for course-related group work or media viewing; arrive on time and restore the room layout before leaving.
cards.short_summary: Reservable library rooms for academic group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson states that library study and viewing rooms are for academic purposes, including group work and course media viewing, and may be reserved one per day for up to two hours.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through SpaceBook, the Service Desk, or phone; one room per day for up to two hours, up to two weeks ahead.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Study and Viewing Rooms
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Book one for course media viewing or group work, then check out the media-cabinet key or remote from the Service Desk if needed.
cards.short_summary: Reservable fourth-floor rooms with media playback equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson says fourth-floor study and viewing rooms support academic group work and media viewing and have VHS, DVD, and CD playback equipment.
cards.access_notes: Reserve one room per day for up to two hours; media-cabinet keys and remotes are checked out at the Service Desk.

cards.title: Fifth-Floor Study and Viewing Rooms
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Use a reservable fifth-floor room when your coursework calls for physical media playback alongside focused group work.
cards.short_summary: Reservable fifth-floor rooms equipped for physical media.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson says fifth-floor study and viewing rooms support academic group work and media viewing and have VHS, DVD, and CD playback equipment.
cards.access_notes: Reserve one room per day for up to two hours; media-cabinet keys and remotes are checked out at the Service Desk.

cards.title: CoLab
cards.subtitle: Iwasaki Library, 120 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Use the movable furniture and writable walls to lay out a collaborative project; confirm availability with the library before planning around it.
cards.short_summary: A flexible library space with writable walls and movable furniture.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson describes the CoLab as a flexible space in the middle of the library with movable furniture and writable walls.
cards.source_title: Get to Know the Emerson Lingo! | Emerson College Human Resources
cards.access_notes: Space availability is managed by the library; confirm current access or reservation needs before visiting.

cards.title: Quiet Lounge
cards.subtitle: Max Mutchnick Campus Center, Piano Row, 150 Boylston Street
cards.notes: Bring independent work to this named lounge in Piano Row, and check the campus-center schedule before depending on it for a session.
cards.short_summary: A named lounge in Emerson’s Piano Row campus center.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies the Quiet Lounge as a space in the Max Mutchnick Campus Center at Piano Row; Campus Centers lists studying among the uses of its social spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located at 150 Boylston Street; campus-center social spaces are for the Emerson community, so check current access before visiting.

cards.title: Beard Room
cards.subtitle: Max Mutchnick Campus Center, Piano Row, 150 Boylston Street
cards.notes: For a planned collaborative session, request the Beard Room through SpaceBook and confirm the reservation before gathering your group.
cards.short_summary: A reservable campus-center room in Piano Row.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies the Beard Room in the Max Mutchnick Campus Center and lists it among campus spaces the Emerson community may reserve through SpaceBook.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required or may be needed; use SpaceBook to select and request the space.
